title: GEOID Sets
text: GEOID sets are collections of Census Geographic Identifiers (GEOIDs) that represent specific geographic areas. GeoIDs.jl allows you to create, manage, and version these sets for consistent geographic area definitions in your analyses.

title: What are GEOIDs?
text: GEOIDs are unique identifiers assigned by the U.S. Census Bureau to identify geographic areas. For counties, a GEOID consists of: The first 2 digits represent the state FIPS codeThe last 3 digits represent the county FIPS code For example, 12086 represents: 12: Florida (state FIPS code)086: …

title: Creating GEOID Sets
text:
You can create a new GEOID set using the create_geoid_set function: # Create a GEOID set for Florida counties
florida_counties = get_geoids_by_state("FL")
create_geoid_set("florida_counties", "All counties in Florida", florida_counties)

# Create an empty set that you can populate …

title: Function Signature
text: create_geoid_set(set_name::String, description::String="", geoids::Vector{String}=String[]) -> Int set_name: A unique name for the GEOID setdescription: Optional description of the setgeoids: Optional initial list of GEOIDs to include in the setReturns: The version number (1 for a new set)

title: Retrieving GEOID Sets
text:
To get the current version of a GEOID set: # Get all GEOIDs in the Florida counties set
fl_geoids = get_geoid_set("florida_counties") To get a specific version: # Get version 2 of the Florida counties set
fl_geoids_v2 = get_geoid_set_version("florida_counties", 2)

title: Modifying GEOID Sets
text: GeoIDs.jl maintains version history when you modify sets. Each modification creates a new version while preserving previous versions.

title: Adding GEOIDs
text:
# Add Collier County to South Florida set
new_version = add_to_geoid_set("south_florida", ["12021"], "Added Collier County")

title: Removing GEOIDs
text:
# Remove Miami-Dade County from South Florida set
new_version = remove_from_geoid_set("south_florida", ["12086"], "Removed Miami-Dade County")

text: GeoIDs.jl maintains complete version history for all GEOID sets.

title: Rolling Back to Previous Versions
text:
You can revert to a previous version: # Roll back to version 1
new_version = rollback_geoid_set("south_florida", 1) This creates a new version that matches the specified version's content.

title: Comparing Versions
text: To compare two versions of a GEOID set: comparison = compare_geoid_set_versions("south_florida", 1, 3) The result is a dictionary with keys: added: GEOIDs present in version 3 but not in version 1removed: GEOIDs present in version 1 but not in version 3

title: Deleting GEOID Sets
text: To permanently delete a GEOID set and all its versions: delete_geoid_set("temp_analysis")

title: Set Operations
text: GeoIDs.jl supports standard set operations on GEOID sets, allowing you to combine and manipulate geographic areas in powerful ways. These operations follow the mathematical set theory concepts and create new GEOID sets that can be saved and versioned.

title: Available Operations
text: The package provides four primary set operations: Union: Combines all GEOIDs from multiple setsIntersection: Keeps only GEOIDs that appear in all setsDifference: Keeps GEOIDs from the first set that don't appear in the second setSymmetric Difference: Keeps GEOIDs that appear in exactly one of the …

title: Union Operation
text: The union operation combines all GEOIDs from multiple sets, removing duplicates. union_geoid_sets(set_names::Vector{String}, output_name::String, description::String="") -> Vector{String}

title: Example
text:
# Combine western and mountain counties into a single set
combined = union_geoid_sets(
    ["western_counties", "mountain_counties"], 
    "western_mountain_counties",
    "Combined western and mountain regions"
)

# Combine multiple regions
combined_regions = union_geoid_sets(
    …

title: Parameters
text: set_names: Vector of GEOID set names to combineoutput_name: Name of the new GEOID set to createdescription: Optional description for the new setReturns: Vector of GEOIDs in the resulting union set

title: Intersection Operation
text: The intersection operation keeps only GEOIDs that appear in all of the input sets. intersect_geoid_sets(set_names::Vector{String}, output_name::String, description::String="") -> Vector{String}

title: Example
text:
# Find counties that are both in Florida and coastal
common = intersect_geoid_sets(
    ["florida_counties", "coastal_counties"],
    "florida_coastal_counties",
    "Florida counties on the coast"
)

# Find counties that are in all three sets
three_way_intersection = intersect_geoid_sets(
    …

title: Parameters
text: set_names: Vector of GEOID set names to intersectoutput_name: Name of the new GEOID set to createdescription: Optional description for the new setReturns: Vector of GEOIDs in the resulting intersection set

title: Difference Operation
text: The difference operation (sometimes called "set subtraction") keeps GEOIDs that are in the first set but not in the second set. difference_geoid_sets(base_set::String, subtract_set::String, output_name::String, description::String="") -> Vector{String}

title: Example
text:
# Get all Florida counties that are not coastal
non_coastal_florida = difference_geoid_sets(
    "florida_counties",
    "coastal_counties",
    "florida_inland_counties",
    "Florida counties that are not on the coast"
)

# Get all high population counties that are not in the …

title: Parameters
text: base_set: Name of the GEOID set to start withsubtract_set: Name of the GEOID set to subtractoutput_name: Name of the new GEOID set to createdescription: Optional description for the new setReturns: Vector of GEOIDs in the resulting difference set

title: Symmetric Difference Operation
text: The symmetric difference operation keeps GEOIDs that appear in exactly one of the two input sets (not in both). symmetric_difference_geoid_sets(set1::String, set2::String, output_name::String, description::String="") -> Vector{String}

title: Example
text:
# Find counties that are either eastern or coastal, but not both
exclusive_regions = symmetric_difference_geoid_sets(
    "eastern_counties",
    "coastal_counties",
    "exclusive_regions",
    "Counties that are either eastern or coastal, but not both"
)

# Find counties that are in exactly one …

title: Parameters
text: set1: Name of the first GEOID setset2: Name of the second GEOID setoutput_name: Name of the new GEOID set to createdescription: Optional description for the new setReturns: Vector of GEOIDs in the resulting symmetric difference set

You can chain set operations together to create complex geographic definitions: # Get Florida coastal counties first

    ["florida_counties", "coastal_counties"],
    "florida_coastal_counties"
)

# Get Florida coastal counties that are not in the southern …

title: Persistence and Versioning
text: All set operations create new GEOID sets that are: Stored in the databaseVersioned like any other GEOID setAvailable for further operations or analysis This means you can: Track how your geographic definitions were createdModify the resulting sets with normal GEOID set operationsRoll back changes …

title: Versioning System
text: GeoIDs.jl implements a robust versioning system for GEOID sets, allowing you to track changes, roll back to previous states, and maintain a complete history of your geographic definitions.

title: How Versioning Works
text: Every GEOID set has a version history. When you: Create a new GEOID set, it gets version 1Modify a GEOID set, a new version is createdAll previous versions remain accessible and unchanged Each version is a complete snapshot of the GEOID set at a point in time, with metadata about when and how it …

title: Version Anatomy
text: Each version consists of: Complete GEOID list: The full list of GEOIDs in this versionVersion number: Sequential integer, starting from 1Parent version: The version this was derived fromChange description: Human-readable description of what changedTimestamp: When this version was createdChange …

title: Listing Versions
text: To view all versions of a GEOID set: versions = list_geoid_set_versions("florida_counties") This returns a DataFrame with columns: version: Version numberdescription: Set description (can vary by version)member_count: Number of GEOIDs in this versioncreated_at: When this version was …

title: Accessing Specific Versions
text:
To access a specific version of a GEOID set: # Get GEOIDs from version 2
v2_geoids = get_geoid_set_version("florida_counties", 2)

# Get the current version
current_geoids = get_geoid_set("florida_counties")  # Same as version 0 The version parameter can be: A positive integer: Specific version …

title: Comparing Versions
text:
You can compare any two versions to see what changed: # Compare version 1 with version 3
comparison = compare_geoid_set_versions("florida_counties", 1, 3)

# Print added and removed GEOIDs
println("Added: ", comparison["added"])
println("Removed: ", comparison["removed"]) The result is a dictionary …

title: Rolling Back to Previous Versions
text:
If you need to revert to a previous version: # Roll back to version 2
new_version = rollback_geoid_set("florida_counties", 2) This creates a new version that matches the content of version 2. The original version 2 remains unchanged.

title: Creating New Versions Manually
text:
While most versions are created through functions like add_to_geoid_set and remove_from_geoid_set, you can also create versions directly: # Create a new version with a completely different set of GEOIDs
new_version = create_geoid_set_version(
    "florida_counties",     # set name
    new_geoids,   …

title: Tracking Changes
text: The system automatically tracks what GEOIDs were added or removed in each version. This change tracking enables: Detailed audit history of how geographic definitions evolvedUnderstanding the impact of each changeReconciling different versionsRecreating the exact state of a GEOID set at any point in …

title: Database Schema
text: The versioning system uses three tables: census.geoid_sets: Basic metadata for each versioncensus.geoid_set_members: The GEOIDs in each versioncensus.geoid_set_changes: Records of specific changes (additions/removals)

title: Backup and Restore
text:
The entire version history can be backed up and restored: # Backup all GEOID sets with version history
backup_geoid_sets("geoid_sets_backup.json")

# Restore from backup (defaults to not overwriting existing sets)
restore_geoid_sets("geoid_sets_backup.json")

title: Database Configuration
text: GeoIDs.jl uses PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension to store and manage GEOID sets. The package provides flexible configuration options through environment variables. Note: If you need to install and set up PostgreSQL first, see our PostgreSQL Setup Guide.

title: Environment Variables
text: You can customize the database connection using these environment variables: Environment VariableDescriptionDefault ValueGEOIDS_DB_NAMEDatabase nametigerGEOIDS_DB_HOSTDatabase hostlocalhostGEOIDS_DB_PORTDatabase port5432 Note: The package now uses PostgreSQL's default socket authentication which …

title: Within Julia
text:
You can set environment variables before loading the package: # Set database configuration
ENV["GEOIDS_DB_NAME"] = "my_census_db"
ENV["GEOIDS_DB_HOST"] = "db.example.com"
ENV["GEOIDS_DB_PORT"] = "5433"

# Load package
using GeoIDs

title: Command Line
text: You can set environment variables when running your script: GEOIDS_DB_NAME=my_census_db GEOIDS_DB_HOST=db.example.com julia my_script.jl

title: Configuration File
text:
For a more permanent solution, you can add configuration to your .bashrc, .zshrc, or equivalent: # Add to your .bashrc or .zshrc
export GEOIDS_DB_NAME=my_census_db
export GEOIDS_DB_HOST=db.example.com

title: Connection String Format
text: The connection string is formatted as: postgresql://host:port/dbname For example: postgresql://localhost:5432/tiger This format uses PostgreSQL's default authentication mechanism, which is socket authentication on most development setups.

text: GeoIDs.jl requires a PostgreSQL database with the PostGIS extension. This guide walks you through setting up a local PostgreSQL server on both macOS and Ubuntu.

title: Database Authentication
text: Note: GeoIDs.jl now uses PostgreSQL's default socket authentication which doesn't require username and password on local development setups. This is especially convenient on macOS with Homebrew installations where the user running Julia has permission to connect to the database.

title: Method 1: Using Homebrew (Recommended)
text: Install Homebrew (if not already installed): /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)" Install PostgreSQL: brew install postgresql@17 Initialize the database: initdb --locale=C -E UTF-8 $(brew --prefix)/var/postgres Start PostgreSQL service: …

title: Method 2: Using PostgreSQL.app
text: Download PostgreSQL.app from https://postgresapp.com/Move to your Applications folder and open itClick "Initialize" to create a new serverAdd to your PATH with: echo 'export PATH="/Applications/Postgres.app/Contents/Versions/latest/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc

title: Ubuntu Setup
text: Update package lists: sudo apt update Install PostgreSQL: sudo apt install postgresql postgresql-contrib Verify the service status: sudo systemctl status postgresql Start PostgreSQL (if not already running): sudo systemctl start postgresql Enable autostart on boot: sudo systemctl enable postgresql

title: Installing PostGIS Extension
text: PostGIS extends PostgreSQL with geospatial capabilities, which are essential for GeoIDs.jl to work with geographic data. It adds support for geographic objects, spatial indexing, and geographic functions.

title: Using Homebrew
text:
Install PostGIS: brew install postgis Create a database (if you haven't already): createdb tiger Enable PostGIS extension in your database: psql -d tiger -c "CREATE EXTENSION postgis;"
psql -d tiger -c "CREATE EXTENSION postgis_topology;" Verify PostGIS installation: psql -d tiger -c "SELECT …

title: Using PostgreSQL.app
text:
If you installed PostgreSQL using PostgreSQL.app, PostGIS is typically already included. To verify and enable it: Connect to your database: psql -d tiger Enable PostGIS extension: CREATE EXTENSION postgis;
CREATE EXTENSION postgis_topology; Verify PostGIS installation: SELECT PostGIS_Version();

title: Ubuntu PostGIS Installation
text: Install PostGIS packages: sudo apt install postgis postgresql-14-postgis-3 Note: The exact package name might vary depending on your PostgreSQL version. Replace 14 with your installed PostgreSQL version if different. Create a database (if you haven't already): sudo -u postgres createdb tiger Enable …

title: Spatial Filtering
text: GeoIDs.jl provides powerful spatial filtering capabilities to generate GEOIDs based on geographic criteria. These functions allow you to select counties based on latitude, longitude, distance from a point, or within a bounding box.

title: Basic Usage
text: The main function for spatial filtering is get_geoids_by_spatial_filter: get_geoids_by_spatial_filter(filter_type::Symbol, parameters::Dict) -> Vector{String} filter_type: The type of spatial filter to apply (:latitude, :longitude, :distance, or :bounding_box)parameters: A dictionary containing the …

title: Latitude Filter
text:
Select counties based on their latitude range: # Get counties in southern Florida (below 27° N)
south_fl = get_geoids_by_spatial_filter(:latitude, Dict(
    "min_lat" => 25.0,
    "max_lat" => 27.0
)) Parameters: min_lat: Minimum latitude (decimal degrees)max_lat: Maximum latitude (decimal degrees)

title: Longitude Filter
text:
Select counties based on their longitude range: # Get counties in western United States
western_counties = get_geoids_by_spatial_filter(:longitude, Dict(
    "min_lon" => -125.0,
    "max_lon" => -110.0
)) Parameters: min_lon: Minimum longitude (decimal degrees)max_lon: Maximum longitude (decimal …

title: Distance Filter
text:
Select counties within a specified distance from a point: # Get counties within 100 kilometers of Chicago
chicago_area = get_geoids_by_spatial_filter(:distance, Dict(
    "lat" => 41.8781,
    "lon" => -87.6298,
    "distance" => 100.0,  # kilometers
    "unit" => "km"
))

# Get counties within 50 …

text:
Select counties within or intersecting a rectangular bounding box: # Get counties in the southeastern United States

    "max_lat" => 35.0,
    "min_lon" => -90.0,
    "max_lon" => -80.0,
    "include_intersecting" …

title: Getting Counties by Region
text:
The package provides shortcuts for common regional selections: # Get all counties in the western United States
western_counties = get_western_geoids()

# Get all counties in the eastern United States
eastern_counties = get_eastern_geoids()

# Get counties in southern Florida

title: Getting Counties by State
text:
You can get all counties in a specific state: # Get all counties in California
ca_counties = get_geoids_by_state("CA")

# Get all counties in New York
ny_counties = get_geoids_by_state("NY")

text: Spatial filtering uses PostGIS spatial functions to perform geographic queries: Latitude/longitude filters use the ST_Y(ST_PointOnSurface(geom)) and ST_X(ST_PointOnSurface(geom)) functionsDistance filters use the ST_DWithin function with proper distance unitsBounding box filters use the …

title: GeoIDs.jl
text: A Julia package for managing, storing, and manipulating geographic GEOID sets with versioning support.

title: Overview
text: GeoIDs.jl provides a comprehensive solution for working with Census GEOID identifiers, particularly at the county level. The package enables you to: Create and Manage Geographic Area Sets: Define sets of counties for analysisTrack Changes Over Time: Full version history for every geographic …

title: Prerequisites
text: GeoIDs.jl requires: PostgreSQL database server (version 12 or higher)PostGIS extension (version 3.0 or higher)Local TIGER/Line shapefiles in the GeoIDs.jl/data directory Important: Before using GeoIDs.jl, follow our PostgreSQL Setup Guide to install and configure these prerequisites. Note: …

title: Installation
text:
import Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/technocrat/GeoIDs.jl.git")

title: 1. Set Up the Database
text:
using GeoIDs

# Initialize the database (only needed once)
initialize_database() This will automatically use the local TIGER/Line shapefile from the GeoIDs.jl/data directory and initialize the database schema.

create_geoid_set("florida_counties", "All counties in Florida", florida_counties)

title: 3. Perform Set Operations
text:
# Get counties in Florida but not in South Florida
central_fl = difference_geoid_sets(
    "florida_counties", 
    "south_florida", 
    "central_florida"
)

# Get coastal counties in Florida
coastal_fl = intersect_geoid_sets(
    ["florida_counties", "coastal_counties"],
    "florida_coastal"
)
